newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: New Dutch insider trading law sent to parliament.
newsitem.headline: New Dutch insider trading law sent to parliament.

text.p: A previously announced draft law to prevent insider trading in securities was sent to the Dutch parliament on Friday, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
One of the major changes with the current situation is that trading with insider knowledge becomes punishable regardless of whether any profits were made from the transaction.
The bill no longer defines insider knowledge as secret information but as information which has not been made public and which could affect the price of securities in any way.
Information would be considered to have been made public if it has been provided to third parties, for instance by means of press publications.
The ministry said it had appeared that it was also possible to use insider knowledge while trading in securities which have not been listed yet but will be at short notice.
The new law will therefore also apply to this so-called 'as if and when issued' trade and to trading in derivatives such as options and warrants.
The law also forbids the passing on of insider information to third parties.
Under the new rules bourse-listed companies, and members of their supervisory and management boards, will be obliged to report their transactions in their own securities.
The bill will be debated in parliament at a later stage.
